nodes.name: Racer chassis and tire model
nodes.purpose: Per-update handling for player and racer cars: tire lateral grip from load and slip angle, speed-sensitive steering, drift state, burnout fishtails, yaw assist, traction control and the slow-motion pursuit-breaker handling boost

nodes.name: Racer engine and gearbox
nodes.purpose: Engine speed smoothing, automatic gear selection, shift timers, speed limiter and the nitrous tank that drains while engaged and refills with speed

nodes.name: Police pursuit activity
nodes.purpose: One pursuit per wanted target: heat escalation over time, the arrest meter, line-of-sight loss and cool-down evasion, and the ramming formations that police units try to close around the target

nodes.name: Civilian traffic
nodes.purpose: Density-driven spawning of civilian cars ahead of the camera, despawn validation, and the lane-following speed controller that slows for curves and for blocked lanes

nodes.name: Opponent race driver
nodes.purpose: Target-speed planning for opponent racers on the road network: curvature speed limits, skill scaling, catch-up acceleration and nitrous decisions that feed the throttle and steering controllers

cards.name: Tire lateral grip curve
cards.summary: Cornering force read from load-sensitivity curves picked by slip angle, scaled by a per-axle grip value
cards.behavior: Each tire converts its slip angle to degrees and halves it, so every curve covers a two-degree step and the fractional part blends between two neighbouring curves. Seven curves run from zero to twelve degrees. Past that, the twelve-degree curve applies flat, which caps cornering force. Each curve maps load in kilonewtons, after a 0.8 load factor, over 0 to 10 kN to a force that rises steeply and then flattens, so heavier load gives less extra grip. The result is multiplied by the axle grip scale, a cornering scale of 1000, a grip factor of 2.5 and any temporary grip boost. Undriven rear wheels below 30 mph get a pilot factor of 0.85 that blends up to full grip by 50 mph.

constants.name: slipCurveSpacing
constants.unit: degrees of slip angle per curve, static

constants.name: loadFactor
constants.unit: multiplier on load per update, rate unverified

constants.name: pilotFactor
constants.unit: grip multiplier below 30 mph, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Speed-sensitive steering lock
cards.summary: Maximum front wheel angle shrinks with forward speed, widens under braking, and opens to match rear slip when counter-steering
cards.behavior: The steering lock for gamepad input comes from a ten-entry table spread over forward speeds from 0 to 160: it starts at 40 degrees and falls to 2.9 degrees at the top. Braking and the handbrake widen the lock by up to a 1.45 multiplier, weighted by a speed table. The average of recent stick input scales the lock up to 1.4 times for sustained hard turns. The car tuning slider adds up to 20 percent per unit. When the player steers into a rear-tire slide, the lock grows to at least the rear slip angle so the player can catch the slide. A hard ceiling of 45 degrees always applies.

constants.name: lowSpeedSteeringLock
constants.unit: degrees at zero forward speed, static

constants.name: highSpeedSteeringLock
constants.unit: degrees at top of speed table, static

constants.name: steeringTableMaxSpeed
constants.unit: forward speed in physics velocity units, meters per second assumed, unverified

constants.name: sustainedInputLockBoost
constants.unit: multiplier at full averaged input, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Steering slew rate and input smoothing
cards.summary: Gamepad steering turns the wheels at a capped rate that slows with speed and quickens with fast stick motion
cards.behavior: On a gamepad the front wheel angle moves toward the target at a base rate of 180 degrees per second. A speed table cuts that rate to 0.3 of the base at high speed. A second table measures how fast the stick itself moves and raises the rate up to 3.1 times for snap inputs, averaged over a 0.15 second window. The 0.55 second running average of stick position adds up to 1.4 times more for held turns. The step for one update is the rate times the update time, and the new angle is clamped to the previous angle plus or minus that step. Racing wheels skip the slew limit.

constants.name: highSpeedSteeringSpeedScale
constants.unit: multiplier at top of speed table, static

constants.name: fastStickSteeringBoost
constants.unit: multiplier at highest stick speed, static

cards.name: Post-collision steering reduction
cards.summary: Steering lock drops for one second after a hard impact and recovers along a short curve, less so at high speed
cards.behavior: A collision impulse starts a one-second timer. During it, the steering lock is multiplied by a recovery curve that starts at 0.2 of normal and climbs back to full by the end of the second. The effect fades with speed: the reduction is fully applied at a standstill and vanishes at 70 percent of 170 mph. This keeps a car from spinning itself after a wall hit at low speed while leaving high-speed control intact.

constants.name: initialSteerFraction
constants.unit: fraction of steering lock at impact, static

cards.name: Arcade drift state
cards.summary: A drift value rises fast when sliding with throttle or handbrake and lowers rear grip while a stabilizer torque keeps the slide controllable
cards.behavior: A drift value between 0 and 1 rises at 8 per second while drifting and falls at 2 per second otherwise. A drift starts above 30 mph when the handbrake passes half travel or the body slip angle exceeds 12 degrees. It holds while throttle times steer times slip stays past 12 degrees, or while the player counter-steers into the slide. While the value is above zero, a yaw damping torque opposes rotation, scaled by the slip angle through a stabilizer curve times 4. Rear tire friction comes from a ten-entry table, from 1.1 down to 0.34. Its input sums half the slip angle, half the yaw rate and 4 times the counter-steer amount, all times the drift value.

constants.name: maxRearDriftFriction
constants.unit: rear friction multiplier at zero drift input, static

constants.name: minRearDriftFriction
constants.unit: rear friction multiplier at full drift input, static

cards.name: Burnout and fishtail launch
cards.summary: Wheelspin at low speed starts a burnout that cuts drive traction and steps the car through several fishtail swings
cards.behavior: Below 20 mph, a drive wheel slip above 0.5 starts a burnout. Drive traction is set from a slip-to-friction curve, which ranges from 1.0 at no slip down to 0.65 at high slip, divided by 1.4. The swing count is 6 times the gap between 1.5 and that friction value, and the slipping side adds one more step that sets the swing direction. Each swing lasts 2 seconds before the counter steps down. The burnout ends early when slip stays under 0.5 for one second, or when the car is above 5 mph and turned more than 0.5 radians off its heading. The differential bias follows the burnout traction so the rear steps out.

constants.name: highSlipBurnoutFriction
constants.unit: friction multiplier at highest slip, static

cards.name: Rear yaw assist and handbrake turn
cards.summary: Rear tires get extra friction against yaw to keep the car pointed, except during a deliberate handbrake slide
cards.behavior: Each rear tire gets a friction boost that grows with the car yaw angle, the per-car yaw control value and speed up to 30. The bonus is capped at 0.35, and the road grade adds to it. The boost is skipped while the handbrake is above half and the yaw is still under 20 degrees, so the player can start a slide freely. A sharp handbrake turn below 80 mph with yaw above 0.3 radians adds 0.5 to rear brake force, which produces a fast 180-degree turn. The yaw control fades as the drift value rises. A blown tire has traction scaled to 0.3.

constants.name: yawAssistFullSpeed
constants.unit: speed in physics velocity units, meters per second assumed, unverified

constants.name: handbrakeTurnExtraBrake
constants.unit: brake input added per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Cornering traction control
cards.summary: Drive torque shifts away from the inside wheel when the driven axle slips sideways under power
cards.behavior: When the driven axle slides sideways in the steering direction and torque pushes forward slip, a limit ramps in between 1 and 20 units of forward slip excess. It is weighted again by the steer-scaled slip direction, which ramps in between 1 and 16 degrees. The wheel on the sliding side loses that fraction of drive torque, the other wheel loses half, and the outside wheel gains the same fraction as extra traction. Burnouts lock the differential instead and skip this control.

constants.name: forwardSlipRampEnd
constants.unit: forward slip speed, meters per second assumed, unverified

constants.name: outsideWheelTorqueShare
constants.unit: fraction of limit removed from the other wheel, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Slow-motion breaker handling
cards.summary: During the slow-motion breaker the car gains downforce, steering lock, front grip and less drag, then ramps back over three seconds
cards.behavior: While the player holds the breaker, a blend value is 1. After release it falls to 0 over 3 seconds of simulated time. The blend adds downforce equal to 2 g of the car mass and cuts aero drag by up to 75 percent. It also lerps the steering angle toward 60 degrees times stick input and multiplies front tire friction by 1 plus 0.75 times the steer amount. Drifting refills the breaker gauge at half a unit per second times the drift value, but only above 35 mph with more than 30 degrees of yaw and while the breaker is off.

constants.name: rampOutTime
constants.unit: seconds, used as 1 divided by 3 per second

constants.name: dragReduction
constants.unit: fraction of drag removed at full blend, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: frontGripBoost
constants.unit: friction multiplier per unit of steer input, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Nitrous tank
cards.summary: A normalized nitrous tank drains while engaged, waits for a disengage delay, then refills at a speed-dependent rate
cards.behavior: Nitrous engages only in a forward gear with throttle above zero and at 10 mph or more. Once engaged it stays on down to half that speed. While engaged, the tank of capacity 1 drains by update time divided by the car discharge time, and torque is multiplied by the car boost value. After release, a disengage timer must run out before refill starts. Refill time per full tank blends between a minimum and maximum value as speed moves through the car recharge band. Opponent drivers on catch-up drain at down to half rate and refill at up to twice the rate.

constants.name: catchupRechargeScale
constants.unit: multiplier on refill per second at full catch-up

constants.name: catchupDischargeScale
constants.unit: multiplier on drain per second at full catch-up

cards.name: Automatic gearbox and engine speed smoothing
cards.summary: Gears shift on rpm thresholds with a traction check, downshift delays are shorter, and displayed rpm falls at a capped rate
cards.behavior: The automatic gearbox upshifts when rpm passes the gear shift-up point, but only when all four wheels touch ground and slip less than 4. Downshifts skip several gears when one would still be too low. When coasting, the downshift point moves 65 percent of the way from idle toward the normal point. A downshift starts a shift timer of a quarter of the normal shift delay. Engine rpm may fall no faster than 2.5 thousand per unit of inertia per second, or 15 thousand while shifting above first gear. Each update then blends 55 percent new rpm with 45 percent old rpm. Above the speed limiter start, throttle fades to zero across the cutoff band.

constants.name: coastingDownshiftPercent
constants.unit: fraction between idle and downshift rpm, static

constants.name: rpmFallRate
constants.unit: thousand rpm per second per unit engine inertia

constants.name: rpmFallRateShifting
constants.unit: thousand rpm per second per unit engine inertia

constants.name: newRpmBlend
constants.unit: blend weight per update, rate unverified

constants.name: sportShiftHold
constants.unit: seconds, decays at 2 minus throttle per second

cards.name: Pursuit heat escalation
cards.summary: Heat rises continuously with pursuit time between a floor and a ceiling, and each whole heat level changes the police response
cards.behavior: Outside cool-down, heat grows by the update time divided by the seconds-per-level value of the current pursuit tier. A career progress bucket, capped at 14, scales that time. Heat is clamped between a base and a maximum. Quick races use 1 and 5. The final story chase pins both base and maximum at 6. Each time the integer part of heat changes, the pursuit resets its formation timer, rechecks support units and loads the reward rate for the new level. Pursuit time also pays reward points once for each completed 10-second block.

cards.name: Arrest meter
cards.summary: An arrest timer fills while a slow target sits near a police unit and drains twice as fast otherwise
cards.behavior: While the target is in sight, slower than the tier bust speed and within 15 meters of the nearest police unit on the ground plane, the arrest timer gains a quarter of the update time. Otherwise it loses half the update time, and it never falls below zero. A target that is flashing after a manual reset counts at any speed within six times the distance and fills four times as fast. When the timer passes 5 the target is arrested and the remaining police units are told to leave. The on-screen meter shows the timer times 0.2.

constants.name: bustedFillRate
constants.unit: timer units per second of update time

constants.name: bustedDrainRate
constants.unit: timer units per second of update time

constants.name: meterDisplayScale
constants.unit: display fraction per timer unit, static

cards.name: Line of sight loss and cool-down evasion
cards.summary: After seven seconds unseen the chase enters cool-down, and hiding spots fill the evade meter faster
cards.behavior: The target counts as seen while any police unit saw it in the last 7 seconds. Past that, the pursuit meter switches mode after 2.5 seconds, enters cool-down, and flags a helicopter search check. The evade level is the unseen time plus bonus hidden time, divided by the cool-down time required, which is 60 seconds by default and comes from the tier. Inside a hiding spot, hidden time accrues at three times the update time when the tier gives no multiplier. Being seen again clears the hidden time and records the last known position. The level shows at least 0.05 and evasion completes at 1.

constants.name: hidingSpotMultiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on hidden time per second

cards.name: Box-in ramming formation
cards.summary: Four police units take slots ahead, beside and behind the target, then pull the box tighter as the finisher timer runs
cards.behavior: The box uses four slots relative to the target: 14 meters ahead, 3.5 meters to each side, and 7.5 meters behind. Each slot has a ramming goal. A tightness value, 0.5 by default, sets how far slots shrink once units are in place. As the time-to-finisher ratio grows, slot offsets scale from 1 toward 1 minus a factor of 0.2 plus 0.2 times tightness. The finisher phase lasts 2 seconds by default. Formations collapse only below a tier collapse speed, which is set to 125 km/h for a target that drives aggressively into police.

cards.name: Traffic spawn density
cards.summary: Civilian cars spawn about 200 meters ahead of the camera at a rate set by density, with oncoming bias at low speed
cards.behavior: Traffic density is the race setting as a fraction, or 1 while free roaming, and drops to 75 percent during any pursuit. Density maps through an eleven-step table to a spawn rate that reaches 8 at full density. Spawn points sit along the camera heading, rotated by a small random yaw. Their distance is 200 meters plus or minus 50 plus the camera forward speed. The chance of an oncoming car falls from 1 at rest to 0.5 at 50 meters per second. A point is rejected within 150 meters of any traffic center or 20 meters of any active car on the ground plane.

constants.name: maxSpawnRate
constants.unit: spawn rate multiplier on update time at full density

cards.name: Traffic lane speed control
cards.summary: Civilian cars hold a posted speed, slow for curves with low friction, and brake for blocked lanes from a stopping-distance table
cards.behavior: Traffic cruises at 35 mph on normal roads and 55 mph on roads with four or more lanes. The curve speed limit comes from the square root of friction times 9.8 divided by path curvature. Traffic uses a friction of 0.6 and police use 1.6, so police take corners much faster. When the lane ahead is blocked, a stopping distance runs from 3 to 50 meters across speeds of 0 to 80, scaled up for mass over 2000. The car slows in proportion to the remaining gap. The target speed of a civilian car may exceed its current speed by at most twice the update time, which caps acceleration near 2 meters per second squared. Look-ahead grows from 10 to 30 meters as speed rises to 25.

cards.name: Opponent acceleration and catch-up
cards.summary: Opponent target acceleration blends toward the player car, scales with skill, and doubles at full catch-up
cards.behavior: An opponent plans acceleration by blending the slowest player car toward its own car by a performance bias. The result is scaled by the car multiplier and doubled when a pursuit-mode racer is actively racing, or by 1.5 when the driver is hunting an aggressive target. Skill maps acceleration from 0.65 to 1.0 and speed from 0.85 to 1.0. Cornering scale runs from 0.36 to 0.9. A catch-up value from 0 to 1 maps through four steps to an acceleration multiplier from 1 to 2. Gravity along the forward slope is added at 9.81. Nitrous adds the car boost on top. The result never falls below zero.
